senses.gloss: (b. h.) to join, arrange, lead (the flock); v. next w.

units: <cite ref="Berakhot 31b:23">Ber. 31ᵇ</cite>, a. fr. <he>דִּבְּרָה תורה כלשון ב״א</he> the Torah speaks according to the language of men, i.e. uses metaphors and phrases adapted to human understanding.
<cite ref="Sotah 12b:20">Sot. 12ᵇ</cite> <he>שעתיד לְדַבֵּר וכ׳</he> destined to speak to Divinity.

Ter. I, 2 חרש שדִּבְּרוּ … מְדַבֵּר wherever the scholars use the word ḥērēsh, they mean one who neither hears nor talks. Mekh. Bo 7, end, a. fr. או אינו מְדַבֵּר אלא ב־ or does perhaps the text speak only of—? [מְדַבֵּר as a noun, v. s. v.].

senses.gloss: to hold communion, converse. Mekh. Bo, introd. לא נ׳ עמו וכ׳ the Lord did not hold communion with him outside the capital of Egypt. Ib. fr.
, same, esp. part. f. מִדַּבֶּרֶת being on terms of intimacy with a man.
units: <cite ref="Mishnah Ketubot 1:8">Keth. I, 8</cite> <he>ראוה מד׳ עם אחד</he> (omit <he>בשוק</he>); expl.
<cite ref="Mishnah Ketubot 7:6">Ib. VII, 6</cite> <he>מד׳ עם כל אדם</he> she is intimate with everybody.
<cite ref="Mishnah Ketubot 7:6">Ib.</cite> <he>לכשהיא מד׳ בתוך ביתה וכ׳</he> when her neighbors can hear her voice in moments of intimacy with her husband.
Macc. 11ᵃ דִבֵּר לחוד יַדְבֵּר לחוד the Piel dibber has one meaning (speaking harshly), and the Hif. yadber another.
